title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Cross-examination - Known Falsehood
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal represents an employee in a WSIB hearing. Opposing counsel calls a witness who testifies that the employee was fully healthy. The client leans over and whispers to the paralegal, "That witness is actually right, my injury was completely faked." Can the paralegal aggressively cross-examine the witness to suggest the witness is lying?
options: Yes, the duty of zealous advocacy requires the paralegal to attack any witness the opposing side presents.
No, a paralegal must not cross-examine a witness in a manner that suggests the witness's evidence is false when the paralegal knows it to be true.
Yes, because the client's admission is protected by confidentiality, the paralegal must act as if they didn't hear it.
No, the paralegal must instantly stop the hearing and testify against the client.
questions.explain: Rule 4.01 (Advocacy). A paralegal must not attempt to deceive a tribunal by making a suggestion to a witness in cross-examination that the paralegal knows to be false. Once the client admits the injury is fake (the witness is telling the truth), suggesting the witness is lying is actively misleading the tribunal. The paralegal also faces a mandatory withdrawal situation here due to the client's fraud.
